title: Clockwork orchestrator for time-sliced kernel fusion and NCCL smoothing
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: At scale, our multi-GPU prefill + decode workload exhibits two correlated pain points: (1) poor kernel throughput when frequent small kernels are dispatched serially across ranks for short token windows, and (2) suboptimal NCCL concurrency where collectives either block compute or fail to properly overlap due to bursty arrival patterns. Both hurt tail latency and unit cost for medium-length chat sessions.

Goal: Design and prototype a runtime "Clockwork" orchestrator that coordinates kernel selection, micro-batch timing, and collective smoothing so that: (a) small kernels are fused or aligned across ranks to amortize launch overhead, (b) NCCL collectives are scheduled in evenly spaced windows to increase overlap with compute, and (c) attention-specific optimizations (tiling, fused QKV paths) are applied adaptively based on recent per-request sequence length and KV cache hit patterns.

Scope: This ticket covers runtime design, prototype implementation in the conductor/scheduler, microbenchmarks on p4d-like topology, and an initial gated rollout for dedicated clusters. It does NOT include UI work or SLA changes (separate PM tickets).
acceptance_criteria: Design doc reviewed and approved by Applied ML and Serving Runtime leads
Prototype implemented in conductor scheduler with a feature flag
Microbench shows >=10% improvement in p99 prefill latency and >=8% token/sec throughput uplift on heterogeneous sequence-length mix compared to baseline
NCCL timeline logs show increased overlap (measured as % time NCCL active concurrently with GPU compute) by >=20% for target workload
Automated unit + integration tests added for timing windows and fallback behavior
Rollout plan documented with kill-switch, canary ratio, and observability dashboards
steps: Week 1: Finalize design and kernel fusion heuristics; define APIs between scheduler and kernel selector
Week 2: Implement Clockwork timing wheel and rank-alignment primitive; add scheduler hooks for NCCL smoothing
Week 3: Integrate attention tiling heuristics and adaptive fused-QKV enablement flags
Week 4: Run microbench suite across 8/16/32 GPU setups, collect p50/p95/p99 and NCCL overlap metrics
Week 5: Iterate on heuristics based on benchmarks; add integration tests and feature-flag guard
Week 6: Canary rollout to 5% of dedicated clusters; monitor dashboards and abort if regressions
risks: Incorrect timing heuristics could increase tail latency for very short sessions
Kernel fusion may interfere with independent memory optimizations and increase peak memory usage
NCCL smoothing relies on stable topology; heterogeneous spot preemptions could reduce effectiveness
Fallback complexity: need simple safe path that disables clockwork without restarting runtime
mitigations: Conservative default heuristics and gradual ramp-up via feature flag
Memory safety checks and optional per-model memory cap before enabling fusion
Topology-awareness in smoothing algorithm and detection of preemption-heavy nodes
Implement fast-path kill-switch and metrics alerts to auto-disable on regression
bench_results: Initial microbench on 8xA100-40GB, mixed seq lengths (16/128/512): baseline throughput 1.00x, clockwork prototype 1.09x throughput; p99 prefill down 12%
NCCL overlap metric (fraction of time NCCL active concurrent with GPU compute): baseline 18%, prototype 24% (+33% relative)
Memory overhead from kernel fusion observed at +6% peak resident on long sequences; within acceptable guardrail for dedicated pools
next_actions: Address reviewer feedback on kernel-selector API (see comment by Mei Chen)
Add per-model feature gating and config surfaced to Dedicated ops team
Schedule canary and build observability alerting thresholds for p95/p99 and NCCL overlap
